result.title: Toaster: Nonlinear Memory from Cascaded Linear Memories and Target Propagation
result.summary: Recurrent memories let language models process long sequences with a fixed-size state. Linear memories such as DeltaNet and KDA store one matrix and take one delta-rule step per token. The product of a chunk of such steps has an exact WY form, so they train fast. Deep memories such as TTT-MLP and Titans store a small MLP, which can hold maps that no matrix can, but their update has no WY form. Toaster bridges the two by building on a known fact: a gradient step on a linear layer is a delta-rule write. It builds a two-layer nonlinear memory from two linear memories with an activation between them. We use target propagation to give the hidden memory its values by projecting the output error back through the second memory. Given a chunk's cross-layer signals, approximated once per chunk, each layer can then run on an unmodified delta-rule kernel. Our default runs this kernel on the output layer and updates the hidden layer once per chunk. Running it on both layers gives a better model in our ablation. At matched backbones and training-token budgets, Toaster has lower loss than KDA at all five tested sizes (0.2B-1.6B non-embedding parameters) on both C4 and PG19. Its C4 perplexity also matches or slightly improves on the attention baseline at every size. At 1.2B it is also below Titans. In a 3:1 hybrid with global attention, the Toaster hybrid has the lowest perplexity of the four hybrids tested, and it is 0.18 (C4) and 0.44 (PG19) below the attention baseline. At the largest size, Toaster's mean three-shot accuracy on 13 tasks is 51.84%, compared with 50.52% for KDA and 50.04% for Titans. In length extrapolation, Toaster's loss stays below KDA's up to 20K tokens (5x the training length). On the 145M backbone, at a hidden width matched to Titans' memory, Toaster takes at most 1.33x KDA's training-step time and is 2.8-5.5x faster than the tested Titans configurations at 32K context.

AI.brief_summary: Toaster 用两个线性记忆（DeltaNet/KDA 式 delta-rule）夹一层激活构成两层非线性记忆，并用 target propagation 把输出误差投影回隐藏层以给出其写入值，使每层仍可用加速的 delta-rule 核训练，在 0.2B–1.6B 规模的长序列语言建模上优于 KDA，并在长外推与混合注意力下保持优势。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本循环记忆工作，但其「分块近似跨层信号 + 用输出误差反向投影给隐藏状态定值」可供核查多步 latent 状态的更新与贡献分配监督，以及固定尺寸状态的长度泛化线索；与视觉证据筛选尚无直接联系。
